Pulmonology · published research

Asthma

In 30 adults with difficult-to-control asthma, LED PBM added to 12 weeks of resistance training improved muscle strength, oxygen consumption at the anaerobic threshold, and shuttle-walk distance more than training with sham light. Pulmonary function and asthma control did not differ between groups.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In 30 adults with difficult-to-control asthma, LED PBM added to 12 weeks of resistance training improved muscle strength, oxygen consumption at the anaerobic threshold, and shuttle-walk distance more than training with sham light. Pulmonary function and asthma control did not differ between groups.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Asthma category has 17 titles; a separate asthma exercise-resistance subgroup adds one relevant title. The 18-title set includes four human trials or controlled reports, ten animal experiments, one asthma-COPD-overlap cell model, and three reviews. Reviews summarize primary studies rather than add independent cohorts.

Human and clinical evidence

Earlier human studies include pediatric laser-acupuncture trials and a controlled adult study. Elsheikh et al. reported improved asthma control and reduced airway resistance after laser acupuncture in 72 adults (2019). Dabbous et al. studied 48 children and measured exhaled nitric oxide, while Elseify et al. randomized 50 children to laser acupuncture or control (2017 2013). A newer triple-blind trial randomized 30 adults with difficult-to-control asthma to resistance training with active or sham LED PBM. Active PBM added greater muscle-strength and submaximal exercise gains, but no between-group difference in lung function or asthma control (Costa et al. 2026).

Animal evidence

Ten mouse and rat allergic-asthma experiments commonly report lower inflammatory-cell recruitment, type-2 cytokines, mucus, or airway remodeling. Models and light protocols differ, and these findings do not establish disease control in patients (Silva et al. 2014 de Brito et al. 2022).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One in-vitro asthma-COPD-overlap model measures cellular responses to PBM (Guerra et al. 2024).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The literature includes laser acupuncture, other laser or LED approaches, and LED PBM immediately before twice-weekly resistance training over 12 weeks. Wavelength is the light's color band and influences how far it can travel through tissue. The functional trial does not show improved lung function or asthma control, and no common asthma dose is established.

Interpretation

Functional improvement is supported by one small controlled training study, while patient respiratory outcomes remain uncertain. Earlier reports suggest symptom or biomarker changes but do not use a single protocol. Trials should test whether functional gains improve daily activity, exacerbations, or asthma control.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for added muscle strength and walking capacity when LED PBM accompanies resistance training in difficult-to-control asthma Very low for improving asthma control, lung function, or preventing exacerbations
Publications and records18 titles (17 exact Asthma plus the asthma/exercise-resistance subgroup)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

A recent small triple-blind trial found better strength and submaximal exercise performance with PBM added to training, but not better lung function or asthma control. Earlier asthma studies are small and use different protocols. Larger multicenter trials should confirm functional benefit and test respiratory outcomes over longer follow-up.
